SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #2 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is an aspect of traditional culture? (1 mark)
   A. Rainfall
   B. Traditional food
   C. Rivers
   D. Mountains

2. In traditional culture, what do we call a basket or clay pot made and used by people? (1 mark)
   A. A type of weather
   B. A river
   C. An artefact
   D. A kind of food

3. How can a school show traditional culture? (1 mark)
   A. By stopping all games
   B. By closing the library
   C. By holding a culture day with songs and dances
   D. By locking classrooms

4. What are values? (1 mark)
   A. Types of buildings
   B. Kinds of food
   C. Good beliefs that guide our behaviour
   D. Kinds of money

5. When giving peer feedback, what should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh
   B. Say only bad things
   C. Say something you like and something to improve, politely
   D. Say nothing

6. What are school rules? (1 mark)
   A. Games
   B. Instructions on what we should and should not do
   C. Songs
   D. Lunch

7. Where is soda ash taken from in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Lake Magadi
   B. Kisumu Port
   C. Mount Kenya
   D. Lake Victoria

8. Which is a way of conserving forests? (1 mark)
   A. Burning the forest
   B. Building fires
   C. Cutting all trees
   D. Planting more trees than we cut

9. Which of these is a safe way for a child to take part in economic activities? (1 mark)
   A. Working at night
   B. Working in a quarry
   C. Helping in the school garden
   D. Carrying heavy loads all day

10. What is the raw material for tea? (1 mark)
   A. Sugarcane
   B. Tea leaves
   C. Fish
   D. Cotton

11. Which is a service industry? (1 mark)
   A. A hotel
   B. A cement plant
   C. A sugar mill
   D. A dairy plant

12. Which factor makes a place suitable for a factory? (1 mark)
   A. No workers
   B. Good roads and nearby workers
   C. No roads
   D. No water

13. Why should every sale be recorded? (1 mark)
   A. So that profit disappears
   B. So that money can be checked and accounted for
   C. So that pupils have more homework
   D. So that the project fails

14. What does the project manager do? (1 mark)
   A. Drives the bus
   B. Prints books
   C. Leads the team and makes sure work is done on time
   D. Cooks lunch

15. Which information should you not share with strangers online? (1 mark)
   A. The weather
   B. The name of your favourite fruit
   C. Your home address and password
   D. A joke

16. What does Stop-Think-Share teach? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore rules
   B. Think before you post
   C. Post quickly
   D. Share your password

17. In school life, what is a right? (1 mark)
   A. Something you are allowed to have or do
   B. A rule to break
   C. A punishment
   D. A duty you refuse

18. Which of these promotes peace? (1 mark)
   A. Bullying
   B. Sharing
   C. Fighting
   D. Rumours

19. What is the Kiswahili word for peace? (1 mark)
   A. Rafiki
   B. Shule
   C. Amani
   D. Chakula

20. If you see a pupil being bullied, what should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore
   B. Tell a trusted adult and support the pupil
   C. Laugh
   D. Join in

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Using time words, write a short history of a school that opened in 1985 and built a library in 2000. (3 marks)

22. Describe how to stay safe during a visit to a factory. Give four rules. (4 marks)

23. State three things that spoil peace in school. (3 marks)

24. Name four roles in a school enterprise team and state one duty for each. (4 marks)

25. The sugar factory employs 700 workers and the tea factory employs 400 workers. How many workers are there in the two factories together? Show your working. (3 marks)

26. Plan a class culture day. State five things you would include. (5 marks)

27. Describe how to interview an elder about traditional culture politely. (4 marks)

28. Describe two peace-building activities that a school can carry out. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #2 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Traditional food
   Dressing, food, housing, artefacts, games and ceremonies are aspects of culture.

2. C — An artefact
   Baskets and pots are artefacts.

3. C — By holding a culture day with songs and dances
   A culture day lets pupils share their heritage.

4. C — Good beliefs that guide our behaviour
   Values guide how we behave.

5. C — Say something you like and something to improve, politely
   Kind, helpful feedback improves work.

6. B — Instructions on what we should and should not do
   Rules guide behaviour.

7. A — Lake Magadi
   Soda ash is mined at Lake Magadi.

8. D — Planting more trees than we cut
   Replanting keeps the forest alive.

9. C — Helping in the school garden
   Light safe work under supervision is fine.

10. B — Tea leaves
   Tea is made from tea leaves.

11. A — A hotel
   Hotels provide services.

12. B — Good roads and nearby workers
   Transport and workers matter.

13. B — So that money can be checked and accounted for
   Records show that money was handled honestly.

14. C — Leads the team and makes sure work is done on time
   The manager coordinates the work.

15. C — Your home address and password
   Private details must be kept safe.

16. B — Think before you post
   We should think about whether it is true, kind and safe.

17. A — Something you are allowed to have or do
   Rights are things we are allowed, such as learning.

18. B — Sharing
   Sharing builds trust and friendship.

19. C — Amani
   Amani means peace.

20. B — Tell a trusted adult and support the pupil
   Reporting helps to stop bullying.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: The school was opened in 1985. Later, in 2000, a library was built. Today, pupils read books in the library.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dates, 1 mark for order, 1 mark for time words.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Stay with the group, do not touch machines, listen to the guide, and wear safety clothing if given.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Bullying, fighting and spreading rumours. Accept stealing or discrimination.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Project manager leads the team, treasurer keeps money records, production team makes the goods, sales team sells the goods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each role and duty pair.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1,100 workers.
   Working / marking points: 700 + 400 = 1,100. 1 mark for adding, 1 mark for correct sum, 1 mark for the unit.

26. (5 marks)
   Answer: Traditional dress, foods to taste, songs and dances, artefacts on display, and stories told by elders.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct item.

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: Greet the elder respectfully, ask permission before recording or taking photographs, listen without interrupting, and say thank you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

28. (4 marks)
   Answer: A peace garden where pupils can sit calmly and a peace poster competition to teach about peace. Explain how each helps.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each activity and 1 mark for each explanation.
